evidence.requirements: Met: list page with heading, Search and Family controls, count text and name links (index.html:18-49, app.js:47-58; list.jpg); search uses alternative names (catalog.js:28-37). Detail view has the facts, the capacity source link, grouped Symbol/Value/Unit tables, Print and 'All cartridges', and a #/cartridge/<key> route (app.js:123-158, catalog.js:57-74). Tolerances appear inline (format.js:109-117; '39.62 -0.2' in detail-308_win.jpg). Angles appear as 40° and 10°58'00". The title block has name, table, revision date, 'Dimensions in mm' and the scale (drawing.js:243-258). Missing values are noted (geometry.js:296-306; 'Note: extractor groove not drawn' in detail-9_3_x_74_r.jpg). Print is one A4 page with a footer (print-308_win.jpg). Partly met: (1) α gets only a leader label (drawing.js:226-232; README:48). It has no dimension line, arrowheads or extension lines, although the brief asks for them. (2) 'Labels do not overlap' fails on 44 Rem. Mag.: the note text runs into the title block (detail-44_rem_mag.jpg). (3) 'Scales to a phone and prints legibly': the viewBox is about 170 mm wide for 308 Win. At 360 px that gives 3 mm labels of roughly 6 px, so phone legibility is doubtful (inferred from code; no phone screenshot).
evidence.correctness: Rim type (geometry.js:42-57) and the chamfer min(f·tanβ, R1/4) (340-347) follow the rules. Groove floor and ramp (354-373) and the belt ramp at δ to R3/2 then E (358-364) are correct; for 300 WM the ramp ends at z≈3.24 < E 5.59. Rimfire half-round radius min(R/2,(R1−P1)/2) has its outermost point at R1/2 (326-337). Bottleneck shoulder fillets use r1 min and r2 (381-393). Seating depth and k by shape and category, with rimfire treated as rifle (211-223), are correct. So are the tangent ogive ρ and centre (176-186), the quarter ellipse, the flat cone and the SWC cone with m=0.6·G1 (188-200). Heeled exposed bullet uses H2 and the heel H2−2tb (439-440). Walls are tn/tb with linear blend across the shoulder, w = max(...) is right, and pocket sizes are correct (19-27, 403-433). Outlines match the reference proportions for 308, 300 WM, 9 mm and 22 LR (shoulder position, neck length, bullet length; 300 WM belt and 22 LR heel visible). Defects: α has no angular dimension; the 44 Rem. Mag. note overlaps the title block; the print footer reads '308 Win..' with a double period (app.js:148; print-308_win.jpg). The diameter extension lines run horizontally across the case and bullet to columns past the tip. This is unconventional against the reference drawings, which dimension diameters at the feature. Print fits one A4 page (print-308_win.jpg).
evidence.security: Data reaches the DOM through textContent/createElement (app.js:23-36). The only innerHTML is the SVG string (app.js:117-121), and every text in it passes through escapeXml (drawing.js:63-69, 321, 334, 338-345). The rest is numbers and internal class names. No eval and no network requests; a browser test checks that only file: URLs load (app.test.js:46). Capacity links go out only when clicked and carry rel=noopener.
evidence.code_quality: Clean split into pure UMD modules (format, catalog, geometry, drawing) plus a thin DOM layer in app.js. Names are clear and functions are small (fillet, roundCorners, clipFrom), and buildModel throws a clear error when R1/P1/L3/H2 are missing. Minor issues: buildModel is about 220 lines and handles many concerns, renderSvg has a redundant axis branch (drawing.js:326-330), and the bullet seated polygon is built twice (geometry.js:244 and drawing.js:142). Size is right for the task (~1100 lines of JS).
evidence.tests: Unit tests cover formatting (angles, tolerances, symbols, units), search and filter counts, routes, and data integrity. Geometry is checked against hand-computed values for 223 Rem., 22 LR, 9 mm, 300 WM and 9,3x74R. Across all 25 records the tests check label-label overlap, label-line intersection (Liang–Barsky) and viewBox containment (drawing.test.js:79-102). Browser tests cover file:// loading, no network, search, filter, reload and bookmark, the one-page A4 PDF, print button, dark mode and phone overflow. Gaps: notes and the title block are left out of the overlap test, which is why the 44 Rem. Mag. overlap slipped through. Flat and SWC noses, the chamfer and rebated cases have no geometry tests, and the print test runs for only one cartridge.
evidence.ux_design: Information hierarchy is good: name, then a three-column facts grid, then the drawing, then grouped tables, with tabular numbers (detail-308_win.jpg). The drawing is weaker. On desktop the cartridge fills under half the drawing width (detail-308_win.jpg, detail-300_win_mag.jpg); the rest is diameter columns and the title block. The hatched section walls are barely visible at that size. Six diameter extension lines run across the body and bullet, which is cluttered and makes it hard to see which feature each value belongs to. The note overlaps the title block (detail-44_rem_mag.jpg). Print is dense and orderly (print-308_win.jpg). There is no dark-mode screenshot to judge.
evidence.accessibility: The SVG has role=img and aria-label '<name> drawing' (drawing.js:320-321). Values are also in proper tables with th scope=col/row (app.js:82-98). Search and Family have labels, the count is aria-live, and focus moves to the detail h1 on navigation (app.js:184-187). :focus-visible outlines are styled (styles.css:67-73). lang=en. Muted text #5a6670 on #fbfaf7 is about 5.6:1. Minor issues: the h1:focus outline is suppressed (fine for a programmatic focus target), and the drawing has no long description beyond its name, though the tables carry the same data.
evidence.simplicity: Plain HTML/CSS/JS with no runtime dependencies. Data is a classic script so the app works from file://. The only dev dependency is playwright-core. About 1100 lines of JS and 590 of CSS for a 25-record reference with a computed drawing is proportionate.
evidence.maintainability: README covers how to open the app, how to run tests (including the Chromium install), the file layout and a 'Decisions' list. package-lock.json is present and engines is node >=22. Missing: no CI configuration, no ADR, spec or docs folder, no changelog or versioning approach beyond version 1.0.0, no .nvmrc, and playwright-core uses a caret range (the lockfile pins it). Regression tests are good.
evidence.visual_design: Calm and consistent: system sans, muted greys with one blue accent, uppercase small table headers and tabular numerals, the same across list and detail pages (list.jpg, detail-*.jpg). The drawing style (thin muted dimension lines, light bullet fill, boxed title block) looks finished. Weak points are the small drawing on a wide canvas, faint hatching, and title-block text sizes that differ visibly between short cartridges (9 mm, 22 LR: large) and long ones (308: small) because of fit-to-width.
evidence.layout: Page order puts the most important content first: name, facts, drawing, tables. The tables sit in a three-column grid with uneven gaps where groups differ in length (detail-9_mm_luger.jpg, 'Projectile' isolated). The drawing wastes space: the cartridge sits left and empty columns and the title block sit right. One real overlap: the note runs into the title block (detail-44_rem_mag.jpg). No clipping or horizontal overflow in any screenshot. The print page fits A4 with room left over (print-308_win.jpg).
evidence.usability: Finding a cartridge is one step: type in Search or pick a Family, then click the name. Search ignores case, spacing and accents (catalog.js:19-26). Back link and Print button are at the top. Addresses are bookmarkable and an unknown key shows 'Cartridge not found' with a back link (app.js:172-178). Values are easy to scan. The drawing's diameter labels are far from the features they measure, so mapping a value to the outline takes effort.
evidence.reception: Reloaders and engineers would trust the data presentation: published values unchanged, tolerances inline, units, sources, and a C.I.P. title block. The drawing is recognisably correct in outline and proportion against the OpenBallistics references. Unconventional dimension placement, the missing α angle dimension and the visible text overlap on 44 Rem. Mag. would read as unfinished drafting to a gunsmith or engineer.

unmet_requirements: Shoulder angle α is labelled with a leader only, with no dimension line, arrowheads or extension lines (drawing.js:226-232)
Labels must not overlap: the 'Note: extractor groove not drawn' text overlaps the title block on 44 Rem. Mag. (detail-44_rem_mag.jpg)
Drawing legibility at phone width is doubtful: labels of about 3 mm in a viewBox about 170 mm wide (drawing.js:21-33, 239-241)
Print footer has a double period after names ending in '.' ('308 Win..', app.js:148)
strengths: Geometry follows the brief's rules closely for every family: chamfer, groove, belt ramp at δ, rimfire half-round, fillets, ogive and nose shapes, heeled bullet, walls, pocket. Missing values are noted, not invented, and outlines match the reference proportions.
Clean, dependency-free, file://-safe architecture of pure, testable modules, with safe DOM construction and escaped SVG.
Solid tests: label-overlap and line-intersection checks over all 25 drawings, hand-checked geometry, and browser tests for file://, routing, the one-page A4 print, dark mode and phone width.
issues: Drawing layout is weak: diameter dimensions sit in columns past the tip, with extension lines drawn across the case and bullet. The cartridge fills under half the drawing width, so the hatched section is faint and labels will be tiny on a phone.
The α angle has no angular dimension, and the 44 Rem. Mag. note overlaps the title block; the overlap tests do not cover notes or the title block.
Maintainability gaps: no CI, no ADR or spec docs, no versioning or changelog, no pinned Node version file.
review.verdict: A careful, well-tested, dependency-free implementation whose geometry follows the brief's rules and matches the reference proportions, with clean tables and a one-page print. The drawing's drafting is unconventional and partly unfinished (far-off diameter columns, no α dimension, a visible text overlap), so it needs one more pass before publishing to engineers.
